title: Codfish Salad, Puerto Rican Style, Serenata

content.title: About
content.content: Codfish salad "Serenata" is a traditional Puerto Rican dish made from boiled or baked cod, pickled vegetables, olive oil, vinegar, and aromatic spices. It is served cold, often as an appetizer or light meal.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cod is one of the most popular fish in the Caribbean due to its mild flavor and low fat content.
The classic "Serenata" recipe includes pickled onion, sweet pepper, and olives, giving the dish a vivid color palette.
In Puerto Rico the salad is frequently served at celebrations and family gatherings, accompanied by "pan de agua" or rice.
The name "Serenata" comes from the Spanish word for "serenade" and reflects the dish's light, refreshing character.
Regional variations may add mango or pineapple for extra sweetness.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Cod provides EPA and DHA, which support heart and brain health.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: The dish fits well into calorie‑controlled diets thanks to cod's low energy density and high protein.

items.title: Source of vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 is essential for nervous system function and red blood cell formation.

items.title: Contains selenium
items.content: Selenium acts as an antioxidant, protecting cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: Vinegar acidity and fresh vegetables promote healthy digestion.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: People allergic to seafood may experience reactions when consuming cod.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Pickled ingredients can raise sodium levels; those with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Heavy‑metal contamination risk
items.content: Cod caught in polluted waters may contain mercury; choose reputable suppliers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the salad chilled, either on a separate plate or atop lettuce leaves. It pairs well with bread, toast, or rice. For extra zing, add fresh lime juice or a dash of chili.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or discoloration.
